method: All inherited current-source and supplemental fingerprints were compared against both frozen trees. The first tree exactly matches the prior completed report; the second differs only in the four manually reviewed files. Fresh imports of each tree reproduce all 204 previous hashes and calculate current hashes independently. Raw source snapshots preserve both sides of each changed file. No live main-worktree product source, content review record or business code was modified.

finalSearchDeltaReview.scope: Exact four-file source delta against the first frozen snapshot: pageTitle/all-published-page directory support, requiresAll and new intent vocabulary, and the Escape close handler. The complete current engine, client and generator were read; the concept additions were read with the verified unchanged prior definitions. Supporting target prose and publishedPages helper were reread. No product edits were made by this reviewer.

evidence.judgement: Removing the docs/article filter includes the already registered published home, examples and blog-list pages. The unchanged publishedPages helper still excludes draft docs/articles and requires aligned locale publication. The generator reads real built HTML, retains locale/canonical/H1/description checks and validates aliases, allowing an absent meta value only when expected terms are empty. It adds the decoded HTML title as pageTitle and uses an empty alias array for pages without configured aliases; URLs remain canonical local paths.

pageTitle is an additional text-evidence field weighted 2.5, below visible H1 weight 5. Results still display the real H1/title and return supplied directory URLs; pageTitle does not generate new copy. The new home/examples/blog-list role branches describe actual page types. Existing locale scoping and plain-text rendering are retained.

requiresAll is an AND across groups with OR inside each group, alongside the existing optional requiresAny requirement. Each regex resets lastIndex before testing. The current cardinality definitions therefore require both note and card subjects; optional consumeContext removes the matched context families from residual lexical tokens. These are source semantics, not claims that every natural-language query is classified correctly.

Customization and the Chinese schema-editing family point to real custom-note-type content about fields, front/back templates and model completion. Occlusion-action terms require an image/diagram subject and point to structured image occlusion; no OCR, arbitrary shape support or hosted uploader capability is introduced. Note/card cardinality is a valid product concept, but its selected concepts-page role leaves the minor content gap recorded below.

The six-line addition handles Escape only while the dialog is open, prevents the input default action, calls the existing closeModal and returns. The unchanged close event invalidates pending requests, clears the timer, removes the body state and restores a connected prior focus target or the open button. The new branch adds no strings, does not modify query ranking and leaves existing Ctrl/Meta+K behavior after it. Browser success remains to be independently verified by the parent.

evidence: English customize/customise, multiple/how many and hide/cover families are ordinary task expressions. Their required field/note/card/image contexts preserve the intended technical meanings instead of treating those broad verbs as product claims.

Chinese 自定义、定制、增加字段、几张、对应、遮住 and 隐藏 are natural query variants. Requiring both 笔记/Note and 卡片/Card/Card(s) for cardinality preserves the note/card distinction; the occlusion verbs require an image-related subject. Locale vocabularies need not be mechanically identical to express the same tasks.

The new pageTitle evidence comes from already reviewed localized HTML titles. No visible label, explanatory paragraph or translated placeholder changes. Escape handling adds no user-facing text. A minor usability issue remains because concepts prose does not directly answer the newly targeted one-note/multiple-cards question.

openIssues.description: The new note/card cardinality intent gives concepts a role prior, but this page does not directly explain that one note may generate multiple cards. The cards tutorial provides a concrete two-notes/three-cards explanation. Consider adding a short explanation or a direct link from concepts. This is a destination-content gap, not an assertion about the final browser result order.
